Rozhiv Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kyivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery appears on 1930s Red Army maps, with burials presumably ending in the early 20th century; locals say its tombstones had already been removed by the 1950s, and 1980s residential construction on the site unearthed human bones. According to Rozhiv's mayor, however, some of the original tombstones have survived and an active search for them continues today. The Jewish community here, traced to an agricultural colony founded in 1850, was reduced to just 19 people by 1926 after a 1919 pogrom, and its remaining members were murdered alongside neighboring villages' Jews during the Nazi occupation.
